sanskrit: teṣu pradravamāṇeṣu pāñcālān sṛñjayāṃs tathā vyadrāvayad raṇe droṇas tatra tatra parākramī
english: As they fled in rout, Droṇa, valorous everywhere upon the field, drove off the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas in the battle.

sanskrit: vijitya pāṇḍupāñcālān bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān svaṃ vyūhaṃ punar āsthāya sthiro 'bhavad ariṃdamaḥ na cainaṃ pāṇḍavā yuddhe jetum utsahire prabho
english: Having vanquished the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas, the majestic son of Bharadvāja, that subduer of foes, took his stand once more within his own array and stood unshaken; nor did the Pāṇḍavas dare to conquer him in battle, O lord.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duḥśāsano rājañ śaineyaṃ samupādravat kirañ śarasahasrāṇi parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O king, Duḥśāsana rushed upon Śaineya, scattering arrows by the thousand like a rain-laden thundercloud.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā sātyakiṃ ṣaṣṭyā tathā ṣoḍaśabhiḥ śaraiḥ nākampayat sthitaṃ yuddhe mainākam iva parvatam
english: Though he pierced Sātyaki with sixty arrows and then with sixteen more, he could not make him waver, who stood firm in the fight like Maināka, the mountain.

sanskrit: sa tu duḥśāsanaṃ vīraḥ sāyakair āvṛṇod bhṛśam maśakaṃ samanuprāptam ūrṇanābhir ivorṇayā
english: But that hero covered Duḥśāsana thickly with his shafts, as a spider, with its web, enmeshes a gnat that has blundered into it.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā duḥśāsanaṃ rājā tathā śaraśatācitam trigartāṃś codayām āsa yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: Seeing Duḥśāsana so studded with a hundred arrows, the king urged on the Trigartas against the chariot of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: te 'gacchan yuyudhānasya samīpaṃ krūrakāriṇaḥ trigartānāṃ trisāhasrā rathā yuddhaviśāradāḥ
english: Those doers of cruel deeds drew near to Yuyudhāna—three thousand chariot-warriors of the Trigartas, skilled in battle.

sanskrit: te tu taṃ rathavaṃśena mahatā paryavārayan sthirāṃ kṛtvā matiṃ yuddhe bhūtvā saṃśaptakā mithaḥ
english: They surrounded him with a vast host of chariots, having steadied their resolve for the fight, bound to one another as sworn confederates unto death.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prayatatāṃ yuddhe śaravarṣāṇi muñcatām yodhān pañcaśatān mukhyān agrānīke vyapothayat
english: As they strove in the fight and loosed their showers of arrows, he crushed five hundred of their foremost warriors in the front of the array.

sanskrit: te 'patanta hatās tūrṇaṃ śinipravarasāyakaiḥ mahāmārutavegena rugṇā iva mahādrumāḥ
english: Swiftly slain by the shafts of the chief of the Śinis, they fell like great trees shattered by the force of a mighty gale.

sanskrit: rathaiś ca bahudhā chinnair dhvajaiś caiva viśāṃ pate hayaiś ca kanakāpīḍaiḥ patitais tatra medinī
english: With chariots broken in many parts, with banners, O lord of peoples, and with horses adorned in gold all fallen there, the earth was strewn.

sanskrit: śaineyaśarasaṃkṛttaiḥ śoṇitaughapariplutaiḥ aśobhata mahārāja kiṃśukair iva puṣpitaiḥ
english: With those mangled by Śaineya's arrows and drenched in floods of blood, the field shone, O great king, as though with kiṃśuka trees in full flower.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare yuyudhānena tāvakāḥ trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta paṅkamagnā iva dvipāḥ
english: Slaughtered in battle by Yuyudhāna, your men found no deliverer, like elephants sunk fast in the mire.

sanskrit: tatas te paryavartanta sarve droṇarathaṃ prati bhayāt patagarājasya gartānīva mahoragāḥ
english: Then they all turned back toward Droṇa's chariot, as great serpents flee to their holes in dread of the king of birds.

sanskrit: hatvā pañcaśatān yodhāñ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ prāyāt sa śanakair vīro dhanaṃjayarathaṃ prati
english: Having slain five hundred warriors with arrows like venomous serpents, that hero advanced slowly toward the chariot of Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ naraśreṣṭhaṃ putro duḥśāsanas tava vivyādha navabhis tūrṇaṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: As that best of men went forward, your son Duḥśāsana swiftly pierced him with nine arrows of smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ prativivyādha pañcabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ rukmapuṅkhair maheṣvāso gārdhrapatrair ajihmagaiḥ
english: But that mighty bowman pierced him in turn with five whetted arrows, gold-feathered, fledged with vulture-plumes, and flying straight.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ tu mahārāja prahasann iva bhārata duḥśāsanas tribhir viddhvā punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: And Duḥśāsana, as if laughing, O great king, O Bhārata, having struck Sātyaki with three arrows, pierced him again with five.

sanskrit: śaineyas tava putraṃ tu viddhvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ dhanuś cāsya raṇe chittvā vismayann arjunaṃ yayau
english: But Śaineya, having struck your son with five swift arrows and severed his bow in the fight, went on toward Arjuna, leaving him astonished.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsanaḥ kruddho vṛṣṇivīrāya gacchate sarvapāraśavīṃ śaktiṃ visasarja jighāṃsayā
english: Then Duḥśāsana, enraged, hurled at the departing hero of the Vṛṣṇis an all-steel javelin, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu śaktiṃ tadā ghorāṃ tava putrasya sātyakiḥ ciccheda śatadhā rājan niśitaiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: But that dreadful javelin of your son Sātyaki cut into a hundred pieces, O king, with whetted heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya putras tava janeśvara sātyakiṃ daśabhir viddhvā siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ha
english: Then your son, O lord of men, taking up another bow and piercing Sātyaki with ten arrows, roared aloud like a lion.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu raṇe kruddho mohayitvā sutaṃ tava śarair agniśikhākārair ājaghāna stanāntare sarvāyasais tīkṣṇavaktrair aṣṭābhir vivyadhe punaḥ
english: But Sātyaki, enraged in battle, having bewildered your son, smote him upon the breast with arrows shaped like tongues of fire, and pierced him again with eight all-iron, keen-pointed shafts.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu viṃśatyā sātyakiṃ pratyavidhyata sātvato 'pi mahārāja taṃ vivyādha stanāntare tribhir eva mahāvegaiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Duḥśāsana then pierced Sātyaki in turn with twenty arrows; and the Sātvata too, O great king, struck him upon the breast with three smooth-jointed shafts of mighty speed.

sanskrit: tato 'sya vāhān niśitaiḥ śarair jaghne mahārathaḥ sārathiṃ ca susaṃkruddhaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Then that great chariot-warrior, sorely enraged, slew his steeds with sharp arrows, and his charioteer too with smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: dhanur ekena bhallena hastāvāpaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ dhvajaṃ ca rathaśaktiṃ ca bhallābhyāṃ paramāstravit ciccheda viśikhais tīkṣṇais tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī
english: With one broad-headed shaft that master of the highest weapons cut his bow, with five his hand-guard, with two more his banner and his chariot-lance, and with keen arrows both his flanking charioteers as well.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ trigartasenāpatinā svarathenāpavāhitaḥ
english: His bow cut, his chariot wrecked, his horses and charioteer slain, he was borne away upon his own chariot by the commander of the Trigarta host.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya śaineyo muhūrtam iva bhārata na jaghāna mahābāhur bhīmasenavacaḥ smaran
english: Though Śaineya rushed upon him, for a moment, O Bhārata, that mighty-armed one did not slay him, remembering the words of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: bhīmasenena hi vadhaḥ sutānāṃ tava bhārata pratijñātaḥ sabhāmadhye sarveṣām eva saṃyuge
english: For Bhīmasena had vowed, O Bhārata, in the midst of the assembly, the slaying of all your sons in battle.

sanskrit: tathā duḥśāsanaṃ jitvā sātyakiḥ saṃyuge prabho jagāma tvarito rājan yena yāto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: And so, having conquered Duḥśāsana in the fight, O lord, Sātyaki went swiftly, O king, in the direction whither Dhanaṃjaya had gone.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kiṃ tasyāṃ mama senāyāṃ nāsan ke cin mahārathāḥ ye tathā sātyakiṃ yāntaṃ naivāghnan nāpy avārayan
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Were there in that army of mine no great chariot-warriors at all, who neither slew nor even checked Sātyaki as he went on his way?

sanskrit: eko hi samare karma kṛtavān satyavikramaḥ śakratulyabalo yuddhe mahendro dānaveṣv iva
english: For alone he wrought his deeds in the battle, that hero of true valor, equal in might to Śakra, as great Indra among the Dānavas.

sanskrit: atha vā śūnyam āsīt tad yena yātaḥ sa sātyakiḥ eko vai bahulāḥ senāḥ pramṛdnan puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Or was that path empty by which Sātyaki passed—he, a bull among men, crushing alone the teeming armies?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca yudhyamānānām apakrānto mahātmanām eko bahūnāṃ śaineyas tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And how did Śaineya, one against many, pass out from the midst of those great-souled warriors as they fought? Tell me this, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājan senāsamudyogo rathanāgāśvapattimān tumulas tava sainyānāṃ yugāntasadṛśo 'bhavat
english: Saṃjaya said: O king, the muster of your armies—with chariots, elephants, horse, and foot—grew tumultuous, like the ending of an age.

sanskrit: āhṇikeṣu samūheṣu tava sainyasya mānada nāsti loke samaḥ kaś cit samūha iti me matiḥ
english: Among the daily-gathered hosts of your army, O giver of honor, there was, I think, no muster in the world to equal it.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sma bhāṣante cāraṇāś ca samāgatāḥ etad antāḥ samūhā vai bhaviṣyanti mahītale
english: There the gods, and the cāraṇas assembled together, were saying: 'Surely the hosts upon this earth shall have their ending here.'

sanskrit: na caiva tādṛśaḥ kaś cid vyūha āsīd viśāṃ pate yādṛg jayadrathavadhe droṇena vihito 'bhavat
english: And never was there such an array, O lord of peoples, as the one Droṇa had ordered at the slaying-quest of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: caṇḍavātābhipannānāṃ samudrāṇām iva svanaḥ raṇe 'bhavad balaughānām anyonyam abhidhāvatām
english: Like the roar of oceans lashed by a furious gale was the din in the battle of those floods of troops as they rushed upon one another.

sanskrit: pārthivānāṃ sametānāṃ bahūny āsan narottama tvadbale pāṇḍavānāṃ ca sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: Of the assembled kings, O best of men, there were many—in your host and in the Pāṇḍavas'—thousands and hundreds.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhānāṃ pravīrāṇāṃ samare dṛḍhakarmaṇām tatrāsīt sumahāñ śabdas tumulo lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: Of those furious champions, steadfast in their deeds in battle, there arose a vast and turbulent uproar that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: athākrandad bhīmaseno dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca māriṣa nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dharmarājaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then Bhīmasena cried aloud, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O sire, and Nakula and Sahadeva and the Pāṇḍava, the king of righteousness.

sanskrit: āgacchata praharata balavat paridhāvata praviṣṭāv arisenāṃ hi vīrau mādhavapāṇḍavau
english: 'Come on! Strike! Range about with all your might! For the two heroes, the Mādhava and the Pāṇḍava, have entered the host of the foe.'

sanskrit: yathā sukhena gacchetāṃ jayadrathavadhaṃ prati tathā prakuruta kṣipram iti sainyāny acodayat tayor abhāve kuravaḥ kṛtārthāḥ syur vayaṃ jitāḥ
english: 'So contrive it swiftly that those two may pass with ease toward the slaying of Jayadratha'—thus he urged on the armies; 'were they to fail, the Kurus would gain their end, and we be conquered.'

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ sahitā bhūtvā tūrṇam eva balārṇavam kṣobhayadhvaṃ mahāvegāḥ pavanāḥ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: 'Therefore do you, joined together and swift, churn up at once that ocean of troops, even as the high-rushing winds churn the sea.'

sanskrit: bhīmasenena te rājan pāñcālyena ca coditāḥ ājaghnuḥ kauravān saṃkhye tyaktvāsūn ātmanaḥ priyān
english: Urged on by Bhīmasena, O king, and by the prince of Pāñcāla, they smote the Kauravas in the fray, casting away their own dear lives.

sanskrit: icchanto nidhanaṃ yuddhe śastrair uttamatejasaḥ svargārthaṃ mitrakāryārthaṃ nābhyarakṣanta jīvitam
english: Desiring death in battle, those men of surpassing splendor, for the sake of heaven and for their friends' cause, did not guard their lives with their weapons.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakā rājan prārthayanto mahad yaśaḥ āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā yuddhāyaivopatasthire
english: Even so your men, O king, longing for great renown and fixing their minds upon the noble resolve in battle, drew up only for the fight.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule yuddhe vartamāne mahābhaye hatvā sarvāṇi sainyāni prāyāt sātyakir arjunam
english: And while that turbulent and dreadful battle was raging, Sātyaki, having cut down all the troops, went on toward Arjuna.

sanskrit: kavacānāṃ prabhās tatra sūryaraśmivicitritāḥ dṛṣṭīḥ saṃkhye sainikānāṃ pratijaghnuḥ samantataḥ
english: There the gleams of the armor, made dazzling by the rays of the sun, smote the eyes of the soldiers in the battle on every side.

sanskrit: tathā prayatamāneṣu pāṇḍaveyeṣu nirbhayaḥ duryodhano mahārāja vyagāhata mahad balam
english: While the Pāṇḍavas were thus striving, Duryodhana, fearless, O great king, plunged into that vast host.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tumulas teṣāṃ tasya ca bhārata abhavat sarvasainyānām abhāvakaraṇo mahān
english: That tumultuous clash between them and him, O Bhārata, became a great undoing of all the armies.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā gateṣu sainyeṣu tathā kṛcchragataḥ svayam kaccid duryodhanaḥ sūta nākārṣīt pṛṣṭhato raṇam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: With the armies in such a plight, and himself fallen into hardship, did not Duryodhana, O sūta, wage the battle from the front rather than turn his back?

sanskrit: ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca saṃnipāto mahāhave viśeṣato nṛpatinā viṣamaḥ pratibhāti me
english: This clash of one against the many in that great battle, and a king at that, seems to me a grievously unequal thing.

sanskrit: so 'tyantasukhasaṃvṛddho lakṣmyā lokasya ceśvaraḥ eko bahūn samāsādya kaccin nāsīt parāṅmukhaḥ
english: He who was reared in the height of comfort, lord of fortune and of the world—encountering many alone, did he not turn his face away?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājan saṃgrāmam āścaryaṃ tava putrasya bhārata ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca śṛṇuṣva gadato 'dbhutam
english: Saṃjaya said: O king, O Bhārata, hear of the wondrous combat of your son, one against the many—a marvel, as I relate it.

sanskrit: duryodhanena sahasā pāṇḍavī pṛtanā raṇe nalinī dviradeneva samantād vipraloḍitā
english: By Duryodhana, of a sudden, the Pāṇḍava host in battle was thrown into confusion on every side, as a lotus-pool is churned up by an elephant.

sanskrit: tathā senāṃ kṛtāṃ dṛṣṭvā tava putreṇa kaurava bhīmasenapurogās taṃ pāñcālāḥ samupādravan
english: Seeing the army thus made by your son, O Kaurava, the Pāñcālas, with Bhīmasena at their head, rushed upon him.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaṃ daśabhir mādrīputrau tribhis tribhiḥ virāṭadrupadau ṣaḍbhiḥ śatena ca śikhaṇḍinam
english: He pierced Bhīmasena with ten arrows, the two sons of Mādrī with three apiece, Virāṭa and Drupada with six, and Śikhaṇḍin with a hundred.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca viṃśatyā dharmaputraṃ ca saptabhiḥ kekayān daśabhir viddhvā draupadeyāṃs tribhis tribhiḥ
english: And piercing Dhṛṣṭadyumna with twenty arrows, the son of Dharma with seven, the Kekayas with ten, and the sons of Draupadī with three apiece,

sanskrit: śataśaś cāparān yodhān sadvipāṃś ca rathān raṇe śarair avacakartograiḥ kruddho 'ntaka iva prajāḥ
english: with fierce arrows in the battle he hewed down hundreds of other warriors and their chariots with their elephants, enraged like Death amid living beings.

sanskrit: na saṃdadhan vimuñcan vā maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukaḥ adṛśyata ripūn nighnañ śikṣayāstrabalena ca
english: Whether nocking or loosing, he could not be seen, his bow bent into a circle, as he smote the foe by his training and the power of his weapons.

sanskrit: tasya tān nighnataḥ śatrūn hemapṛṣṭhaṃ mahad dhanuḥ bhallābhyāṃ pāṇḍavo jyeṣṭhas tridhā ciccheda māriṣa
english: As he smote the foe, the eldest Pāṇḍava with two broad-headed shafts cut his great gold-backed bow into three pieces, O sire.

sanskrit: vivyādha cainaṃ bahubhiḥ samyag astaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ varmāṇy āśu samāsādya te bhagnāḥ kṣitim āviśan
english: And he pierced him with many keen arrows well aimed; but striking his mail at once they broke and sank into the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ pramuditāḥ pārthāḥ parivavrur yudhiṣṭhiram yathā vṛtravadhe devā mudā śakraṃ maharṣibhiḥ
english: Then the rejoicing Pārthas gathered round Yudhiṣṭhira, as at the slaying of Vṛtra the gods, with the great seers, in their joy gathered round Śakra.

sanskrit: atha duryodhano rājā dṛḍham ādāya kārmukam tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti rājānaṃ bruvan pāṇḍavam abhyayāt
english: Then King Duryodhana, taking up a stout bow and crying 'Stand! Stand!' to the king, advanced upon the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā vādinaṃ rājaṃs tava putraṃ mahāratham pratyudyayuḥ pramuditāḥ pāñcālā jayagṛddhinaḥ
english: As your son, that great chariot-warrior, spoke thus, O king, the Pāñcālas, rejoicing and greedy for victory, went forth to meet him.

sanskrit: tān droṇaḥ pratijagrāha parīpsan yudhi pāṇḍavam caṇḍavātoddhutān meghān sajalān acalo yathā
english: These Droṇa held in check, seeking to win the Pāṇḍava in the fight, as a mountain holds the water-laden clouds driven up by a raging wind.

sanskrit: tatra rājan mahān āsīt saṃgrāmo bhūrivardhanaḥ rudrasyākrīḍasaṃkāśaḥ saṃhāraḥ sarvadehinām
english: There, O king, was a great combat that swelled vastly, like the playground of Rudra, a destruction of all embodied beings.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca aparāhṇe mahārāja saṃgrāmaḥ samapadyata parjanyasamanirghoṣaḥ punar droṇasya somakaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: In the afternoon, O great king, the combat broke out anew, loud as a thundercloud, between Droṇa and the Somakas.

sanskrit: śoṇāśvaṃ ratham āsthāya naravīraḥ samāhitaḥ samare 'bhyadravat pāṇḍūñ javam āsthāya madhyamam
english: Mounting his chariot drawn by red steeds, that hero among men, composed, rushed in the battle upon the Pāṇḍavas at a moderate speed.

sanskrit: tava priyahite yukto maheṣvāso mahābalaḥ citrapuṅkhaiḥ śitair bāṇaiḥ kalaśottamasaṃbhavaḥ
english: Devoted to your welfare and weal, that mighty bowman of great strength, born from the noblest of pitchers, with whetted arrows of variegated feathers—

sanskrit: varān varān hi yodhānāṃ vicinvann iva bhārata akrīḍata raṇe rājan bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān
english: singling out, as it were, the choicest among the warriors, O Bhārata—the majestic son of Bharadvāja, O king, sported in the battle.

sanskrit: tam abhyayād bṛhatkṣatraḥ kekayānāṃ mahārathaḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ vīrapañcānāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ samarakarkaśaḥ
english: Against him came Bṛhatkṣatra, the great chariot-warrior of the Kekayas, eldest of five heroic brothers, hardened in battle.

sanskrit: vimuñcan viśikhāṃs tīkṣṇān ācāryaṃ chādayan bhṛśam mahāmegho yathā varṣaṃ vimuñcan gandhamādane
english: Loosing keen arrows and thickly covering the preceptor, as a great cloud loosing rain upon Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo mahārāja svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān preṣayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ sāyakān daśa sapta ca
english: At him Droṇa, O great king, in fury sent seventeen gold-feathered shafts whetted upon stone.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu droṇadhanurmuktān ghorān āśīviṣopamān ekaikaṃ daśabhir bāṇair yudhi ciccheda hṛṣṭavat
english: But those dread shafts loosed from Droṇa's bow, like venomous serpents, he cut each one with ten arrows in the fight, as though delighting in it.

sanskrit: tasya tal lāghavaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahasan dvijasattamaḥ preṣayām āsa viśikhān aṣṭau saṃnataparvaṇaḥ
english: Seeing that deftness of his, the best of the twice-born, smiling, sent eight smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā patataḥ śīghraṃ droṇacāpacyutāñ śarān avārayac charair eva tāvadbhir niśitair dṛḍhaiḥ
english: Seeing those arrows sped from Droṇa's bow swiftly descending, he warded them off with just as many sharp and stout arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavan mahārāja tava sainyasya vismayaḥ bṛhatkṣatreṇa tat karma kṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā suduṣkaram
english: Then, O great king, there came wonder upon your army, beholding that most arduous feat performed by Bṛhatkṣatra.
